guide_enrichment.narrative:
We are not reacting to either team’s latest loss. Temple rushed for 270 yards at Toledo and held a two-touchdown lead late, while Army carried a double-digit fourth-quarter lead against South Florida. The useful takeaway is that Temple has produced at least 186 rushing yards in every game, giving it a credible way to sustain possessions and keep this competitive. The concern is that Army has allowed only 98.5 rushing yards per game, so Temple’s clearest offensive strength runs into meaningful resistance.

Where this gets interesting is on the other side. Our matchup data gives Army an advantage both on the ground and through the air against Temple’s defense. Army is averaging 394 rushing yards per game and has already generated 25 runs of at least 10 yards, while Temple has allowed opponents to convert more than half of their third downs. Cale Hellums also completed 9 of 10 passes against South Florida, so Temple cannot focus exclusively on the run. Our numbers still make the teams closer than the market does, but Army’s favorable offensive matchup and the cost attached to the available number leave us without enough value to move beyond a pass.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: For us, the matchup to watch is Army’s offense against Temple on early downs. Hellums, Godspower Nwawuihe and Zach Mundell give Army multiple rushing threats, and the offense has avoided an interception through two games while allowing very little backfield disruption. If Temple cannot force longer-yardage situations, Army can control possession and limit the number of chances Temple gets to exploit its own rushing game. That is the clearest challenge to our more favorable view of Temple.

guide_extractions.document_match_reason: The guide is Army's Week 4 game notes for its Sept. 25, 2026 road game against Temple at Lincoln Financial Field.

recent_game.fact: Army lost 28-24 to South Florida on Sept. 12, falling to 1-1 overall and 0-1 in the American Conference.
Quarterback Cale Hellums completed 9 of 10 passes for 91 yards and two touchdowns against South Florida; his .900 completion percentage was a career high.
Godspower Nwawuihe led Army against South Florida with 20 carries for 98 yards and scored on a 10-yard fourth-quarter run.
Zach Mundell caught three passes against South Florida, including a 24-yard touchdown from Cale Hellums, and completed a 37-yard pass to Godspower Nwawuihe.

opponent_notes.fact: Temple enters the matchup 1-2 overall and has not yet played an American Conference game in 2026.
Temple is averaging 31.67 points, 359.0 total yards, 221.3 rushing yards and 137.67 passing yards per game.
Temple is allowing 30.0 points and 414.7 total yards per game, including 297.33 passing yards and 117.3 rushing yards per game.
K.C. Keeler is in his second season as Temple's head coach; Temple went 5-7 overall and 3-5 in conference play in 2025.

quarterback.fact: Senior Cale Hellums is listed as Army's first-team quarterback, ahead of Bryson Luter and Ethan Washington.
Hellums returned as Army's starting quarterback after making 10 starts and appearing in every game in 2025.
Hellums rushed for 1,223 yards and 18 touchdowns in 2025; the touchdown total was second in Army single-season history.
Through two games in 2026, Hellums has 150 passing yards, 142 rushing yards and a team-high four total touchdowns.
Against Bryant, Hellums rushed seven times for 87 yards and two touchdowns and completed 4 of 9 passes for 59 yards.

offensive_personnel.fact: Army's listed first-team offensive line is left tackle Henry Appleton, left guard Kyle Kloska, center Brady Small, right guard Paolo Gennarelli and right tackle Teddy Williams.
Army's listed second-team offensive linemen are Xavier Archawski at left tackle, Ben Britton at left guard, Chuck Johnson at center, Sam Waters at right guard and Brandon Wraalstad at right tackle.
Godspower Nwawuihe is listed as the first-team running back, with Jake Rendina and Carson Smith behind him.
Senior Samari Howard is listed as the first-team slotback, with Zach Mundell and David Clerk also on the slotback depth chart.
Army lists Parker Poloskey as its first-team tight end and Brady Anderson as its first-team wide receiver.
Nwawuihe has emerged as Army's feature back after his performance in the 2025 Fenway Bowl and has 147 rushing yards and three total touchdowns through two games.
Mundell has 150 rushing yards and three total touchdowns through two games after playing only his second game since 2023 in the opener against Bryant.

defensive_personnel.fact: Army's listed first-team defensive front consists of Dillon Stowers at defensive tackle, Kody Harris-Miller at nose tackle and Jack Bousum at defensive end.
Army lists Noah Nixon at outside linebacker, Jaquavious Moss and Elijah Walton at inside linebacker, and Zane Tallman at nickelback.
Army's listed first-team secondary is cornerbacks Jaydan Mayes and Jaxon Hammond, strong safety Caleb Williams and free safety Stephen Nnadozie.
Elijah Walton and Jaquavious Moss share the team lead with 12 tackles through two games.
Dillon Stowers leads Army with one sack, while Zane Tallman has the team's only forced fumble through two games.

coaching_changes.fact: John Holt is in his first season as Army's co-offensive line coach, working with third-year co-offensive line coach Cheston Blackshear.
Jamere Hogue is in his first season as defensive line coach, and Munir Prince is in his first season as cornerbacks coach.
Cody Worley remains Army's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach, while Daryl Dixon remains defensive coordinator and Scot Sloan is the co-defensive coordinator and safeties coach.

recent_game.fact: Temple lost 49-48 in overtime at Toledo after its attempt at a game-winning two-point conversion fell incomplete.
Temple led Toledo 42-28 with 6:40 remaining, but Toledo scored twice in the final 1:05 and recovered an onside kick before winning in overtime.
Temple rushed for 270 yards against Toledo, its third consecutive game with at least 176 rushing yards.
In his first game action for Temple, Sam Brown rushed for a career-high 109 yards and scored three combined touchdowns against Toledo.
Kevin Hornbeak forced a fumble on Toledo's first offensive play, and Saboor Karriem recovered it.

opponent_notes.fact: Army enters the matchup 1-1 overall and 0-1 in American Conference play after a Week 3 bye.
Army opened the season with a 59-3 win over Bryant and rushed for 569 yards; five players had at least 53 rushing yards.
Slotback Zach Mundell led Army against Bryant with 105 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
Army lost 28-24 to South Florida after holding a 24-14 lead with 10:56 remaining in the fourth quarter.
Against South Florida, Army punted with 3:10 remaining, allowed a 10-play, 81-yard game-winning drive, and fumbled on its final possession.

quarterback.fact: Ajani Sheppard threw the first touchdown pass of his career against Toledo, a two-yard fourth-down score to Joey Schlaffer.
Sheppard connected with Colin Chase for a 69-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter against Toledo and later scored on a 22-yard overtime run.
Penn State transfer Jaxon Smolik and Washington State transfer Ajani Sheppard entered 2026 as Temple's two primary quarterbacks with limited previous playing experience.

Temple added defensive linemen Kevin Hornbeak Jr., Kaleb Artis, Davier Bishop, Quante Gillians, Deshon Dodson and Lamar Fairfax through the transfer portal.
Temple added outside linebackers Jaylon Joseph from Lafayette and JaMair Diaz from Sam Houston.
